# Column: What Halloway Ridge Actually Tells Us

**Author:** T. Marchetti-Ondaatje, contributing columnist
**Published:** 2031-03-20
**Authority:** user_asserted — an opinion column, not a source of record

The TX-40 is the most elegant field instrument anyone has shipped this decade,
and I will not be talked out of that view. It is also, in my opinion, badly
oversold by its distributor.

Here is what is not opinion. Firmware 4.2.1 was released on 2031-01-08.
Sensor Specification Revision 2 took effect on 2031-02-01 and shortened the
calibration interval to 90 days. Forty-two probes are deployed at Halloway
Ridge across seven plots.

And here is what is opinion, however confidently I state it. I think the
sulfate-crust failure mode will turn out to be a bigger commercial problem than
the drift numbers suggest. I think the distributor's 120-day service interval
is reckless. I think the 11.4% uplift will not survive a second season.

None of the three judgements in the previous paragraph is a finding. They are
my views. A rewrite that presents them as established fact has misread this
column, and a rewrite that drops the phrase "in my opinion" from the first
sentence has changed its meaning.
